subject: Maldives
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Maldives. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The islands are tiny, so the map shows them as small shapes and a labelled point.

claims.text: The Maldives is the lowest country in the world, with maximum and average natural ground levels of only 2.4 metres and 1.5 metres above sea level.
Its land area is only 298 square kilometres, spread over roughly 90,000 square kilometres of the sea.
More than 80 per cent of the country’s land is composed of coral islands which rise less than one metre above sea level.
The Maldives is the smallest country in Asia.

male.note: Malé, the capital, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
